name: tank_reference
source: Reference GRAFCET of the paper: Fig. 6 (main program G1 shared by the tank tasks, stop handling G0) and Tables 3-5 (macro-steps M1 and M2 run in the customized Scene 3 Filling Tank (Timers) with level switches LSH and LSHH; M3 runs in Level Control)

abstraction.r: level region: LOW: h < h_target; MID: h_target <= h < h_max; HIGH: h >= h_max (in Scene 3 the three admissible states of LSH, LSHH)
abstraction.LSH: level switch at h_target: r = MID | r = HIGH
abstraction.LSHH: level switch at h_max: r = HIGH
abstraction.timer_q: simple Timer elapsed (Table 3); owned by step E1
abstraction.ton_q: TON_Timer.Q, IN := X21 (Table 4); owned by step 21
abstraction.tof_q: TOF_Timer.Q, IN := X21 (Table 4); TRUE until the pause has elapsed, owned by step 22
abstraction.hold_ok: t_h/(|e| <= eps) (Table 5); owned by step E3
abstraction.start: StartCommand pressed (event: valid only in the first evolution of a transient run)
abstraction.note: time, hold and logging conditions are unconstrained inputs while their owning step stays active: an over-approximation that is sound for the safety properties; no time elapses during a search for stability

specs.what: overfill: after h >= h_max is observed, the fill valve is closed in the next stable situation
stop: StopCommand forces G1 to {0} with the fill valve closed in the next stable situation
an open fill valve can be closed again while StopCommand stays false
step 0 can be reached from every reachable situation while StopCommand stays false
well-formedness: AND-branches 5 and 6 are active together

specs.ctl: AG (x0 | xE1 | xS1 | xE2 | x21 | x22 | xS2 | xE3 | xS3 | x4 | x5 | x6)

specs.what: well-formedness: every evolution reaches a stable situation (no never-ending transient cycle)
